hydrate()

The hydrate() method declares a deferred factory as the authoritative initial state source for a FeatureCell. It provides a deterministic mechanism for resolving dynamic or runtime-derived data during initialization.

Method Contract Summary

  • hydrate() is optional
  • hydrate() must be called before initialize()
  • hydrate() has highest initialization precedence
  • hydrate() does not execute until initialize() is called
  • hydrate() integrates directly with the core pipeline

When declared, hydrate() overrides Persist behaviors and descriptor.initialState. It represents an explicit decision to derive initial state from a runtime-evaluated source.

What hydrate() Does

Calling hydrate(factory) registers a deferred factory that will be executed during the initialization cycle.

The factory may:

  • Return a value synchronously
  • Return a Promise that resolves asynchronously
  • Return undefined
  • Throw an error

hydrate() does not immediately execute the factory. The factory runs only when initialize() is called.

Configuration
hydrate()
Method Description
hydrate(factory)

inputs:

  • DeferredType<T>

returns:

  • CellBuilderContract<T>
Registers a deferred factory as the authoritative initialization source. Must be called before initialize().
Execution Model

During initialization, hydrate() is evaluated first. No other initialization source is considered.

If the factory produces a value, that value is enqueued as a standard replaceState operation and processed through the full pipeline:

  • Resolve
  • Operators
  • Filters
  • Reducers
  • Emit

Initialization is not a direct mutation. The hydrated value is subject to all installed pipeline logic.

Diagram
Resolution Outcomes
hydrate() Resolution Outcomes
Factory Result Behavior
Returns value Value is processed as a replaceState operation through the full pipeline.
Resolves to undefined No write occurs. FeatureCell remains with value: undefined and hasValue: false.
Throws Initialization fails. No fallback source is evaluated. The error is emitted.

Undefined resolution is not treated as failure. A thrown error is treated as an initialization failure because the declared authoritative source did not resolve successfully.

Why hydrate() Has Highest Precedence

hydrate() represents an explicit request for dynamic, runtime-derived data. When declared, the engineer is intentionally choosing fresh or computed state over previously persisted or statically configured values.

Persisted storage may contain stale data. descriptor.initialState is static by definition. hydrate() communicates that neither of those sources should be considered authoritative for this initialization cycle.

If dynamic resolution is not desired, do not declare hydrate(). Vault will then evaluate storage or static configuration according to precedence rules.

Core Fluent API

hydrate() is a core fluent API method provided by FeatureCell. It does not require additional Behaviors to be registered on the FeatureCell declaration.

The Resolve stage already includes built-in support for deferred factories and Promise-based inputs. hydrate() integrates directly with this core capability.

No custom resolve behavior is required. No special configuration is necessary beyond calling hydrate() before initialize().

Examples

Example: Asynchronous Hydration

{{`
@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .hydrate(() =>
        fetch('/api/employees')
          .then(res => res.json())
      )
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}

Example: Synchronous Hydration

{{`@FeatureCell<Employee[]>('employees')
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault<Employee[]>(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    this.vault
      .hydrate(() => [
        { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
        { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
      ])
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}

Example: Synchronous Hydration

{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell({
  key: 'employees'
});

employeeCell
  .hydrate(() => [
    { id: 1, name: 'Alice' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }
  ])
  .initialize();`}}

Example: Asynchronous Hydration

Failure Model

hydrate() failure occurs only when the factory throws or a returned Promise rejects.

On failure:

  • hasValue remains false
  • value remains undefined
  • error is populated

The pipeline remains operational, but the initialization contract did not resolve as declared.

Recovery, if desired, must be explicit using reset() and replaceState().
